split_rule: Fixed before any retrieval run: 15 dev / 5 test. Test questions are spread over both chapters and include 2 filter questions.
filter_rule: filter.chapter is supplied by the user context before retrieval (e.g. 'I am studying Chapter 2'). Used only by config C; A/B ignore it.

questions.question: What do sociologists call a group of people who live in a defined geographic area, interact with one another, and share a common culture?
questions.expected_answer: A society.
questions.evidence_quote: A group of people who live in a defined geographic area, who interact with one another, and who share a common culture is what sociologists call a society.

questions.question: What is the name for the mistake of treating an abstract idea such as culture as if it physically existed?
questions.expected_answer: Reification.
questions.evidence_quote: The error of treating an abstract concept as though it has a real, material existence is known as reification

questions.question: What term did Norbert Elias use for analyzing individuals and the society that shapes their behavior at the same time?
questions.expected_answer: Figuration.
questions.evidence_quote: German sociologist Norbert Elias called the process of simultaneously analyzing the behavior of individuals and the society that shapes that behavior figuration.

questions.question: Who first coined the term sociology, and was it Auguste Comte?
questions.expected_answer: Emmanuel-Joseph Sieyès coined it in 1780 in an unpublished manuscript; Comte only reintroduced the term in 1838.
questions.evidence_quote: The term sociology was first coined in 1780 by the French essayist Emmanuel-Joseph Sieyès (1748–1836) in an unpublished manuscript (Fauré et al. 1999). In 1838, the term was reintroduced by Auguste Comte

questions.question: What was the first book to have the word sociology in its title, and who wrote it?
questions.expected_answer: The Study of Sociology, published by Herbert Spencer in 1873.
questions.evidence_quote: In 1873, the English philosopher Herbert Spencer published The Study of Sociology, the first book with the term “sociology” in the title.

questions.question: Where and when did Émile Durkheim establish the first European department of sociology?
questions.expected_answer: At the University of Bordeaux in 1895.
questions.evidence_quote: establishing the first European department of sociology at the University of Bordeaux in 1895

questions.question: Which sociologist said people judge themselves by how others react to them, and what did he call this idea?
questions.expected_answer: Charles Horton Cooley; the looking-glass self.
questions.evidence_quote: Calling this idea ‘the looking-glass self,’ Cooley argued that we ‘see’ ourselves by the reactions of others with whom we interact.

questions.question: According to Robert Merton, what is the difference between manifest and latent functions?
questions.expected_answer: Manifest functions are sought or anticipated consequences of a social process; latent functions are unsought consequences.
questions.evidence_quote: Manifest functions are the consequences of a social process that are sought or anticipated, while latent functions are the unsought consequences of a social process.

questions.question: Which technique used theater as an analogy for social interaction, and who developed it?
questions.expected_answer: Dramaturgical analysis, developed by Erving Goffman.
questions.evidence_quote: Erving Goffman (1922-1982) to develop a technique called dramaturgical analysis. Goffman used theater as an analogy for social interaction

questions.question: In the hypothesis 'if unemployment increases, then the crime rate will increase', which is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable?
questions.expected_answer: Unemployment is the independent variable; the crime rate is the dependent variable.
questions.evidence_quote: unemployment is the independent variable and the crime rate is the dependent variable.

questions.question: Which research quality describes how well a study measures what it was designed to measure?
questions.expected_answer: Validity.
questions.evidence_quote: Researchers also strive for validity, which refers to how well the study measures what it was designed to measure.

questions.question: What defines a random sample?
questions.expected_answer: Every person in the population has the same chance of being chosen for the study.
questions.evidence_quote: In a random sample, every person in a population has the same chance of being chosen for the study.

questions.question: Why is the Hawthorne effect unavoidable in some research studies?
questions.expected_answer: Because sociologists have to make the purpose of the study known, so subjects know they are being observed.
questions.evidence_quote: The Hawthorne effect is unavoidable in some research studies because sociologists have to make the purpose of the study known.

questions.question: What did the Frankfurt School develop as an elaboration on Marxist principles?
questions.expected_answer: Critical theory.
questions.evidence_quote: In the 1930s and 1940s, German philosophers, known as the Frankfurt School, developed critical theory as an elaboration on Marxist principles.
questions.filter_note: The Frankfurt School also appears in Chapter 2 (p.52, critical sociology); the filter separates the two.

questions.question: What ethical concern did Max Weber identify for sociological research?
questions.expected_answer: Personal values must not shape interpretation of results; sociologists must establish value neutrality.
questions.evidence_quote: Sociologists, he stated, must establish value neutrality, a practice of remaining impartial, without bias or judgment, during the course of a study and in publishing results
questions.filter_note: Weber also appears in Chapter 1 (p.26 verstehen, p.32 conflict theory).

questions.question: Case studies are rarely a primary method, but in what situation are they especially useful?
questions.expected_answer: When the single case is unique, e.g. a feral child.
questions.evidence_quote: However, case studies are useful when the single case is unique.

questions.question: In the bumper sticker experiment on police treatment of drivers, how many citations did the drivers get and over how many days?
questions.expected_answer: Thirty-three citations in seventeen days.
questions.evidence_quote: After seventeen days, the fifteen drivers had collected a total of thirty-three traffic citations.

questions.question: Whose research did the Supreme Court cite in Brown vs. the Board of Education?
questions.expected_answer: Kenneth and Mamie Clark.
questions.evidence_quote: the Supreme Court cited the research of the husband-and-wife team of social scientists, Kenneth and Mamie Clark

questions.question: Which study investigated whether people can get by on minimum-wage work?
questions.expected_answer: Barbara Ehrenreich's participant observation for her book Nickel and Dimed.
questions.evidence_quote: This type of research is what journalist Barbara Ehrenreich conducted for her book Nickel and Dimed.
questions.filter_note: Minimum wage also appears in Chapter 1 (p.27, public sociology debate).

questions.question: How does qualitative sociology seek to understand human behavior?
questions.expected_answer: Through in-depth interviews, focus groups, and analysis of content sources.
questions.evidence_quote: Qualitative sociology seeks to understand human behavior by learning about it through in-depth interviews, focus groups, and analysis of content sources
questions.filter_note: Qualitative data is also discussed in Chapter 2 (p.54, p.59).
